children: The AfD landslide in the German state of Saxony-Anhalt will pile further pressure on the national government in Berlin and on Chancellor Friedrich Merz's leadership, Commerzbank's Ralph Solveen says in a note. Moreover, the poor showing by the Christian Democrats and Social Democrats is likely to strain the coalition's cooperation and make it no easier to reach agreements on upcoming reforms, he says. However, an AfD government in Saxony-Anhalt won't impact policy areas of greatest interest to financial markets--taxes, social security, and the makeup of the labor market. The AfD promises to advocate for its chosen issues in the federal upper house--the Bundesrat--though it remains ostracized from the mainstream parties, Solveen says. (edward.frankl@wsj.com)
